scope_note: Atomic scene activation slice: construction/replacement/unload and immediate prefab construction share the gameplay journal. Native and preview activation prepare resource plans and publish only after validation and commit. Failed editor reload preserves prior identity/description/residency. Whole-project startup, guarded runtime resource mutations and remaining editor boundaries still keep F2 open. ABI/schema unchanged.
integration_findings: Partial component acceptance is retired for scene and immediate prefab construction: invalid payloads reject the complete activation without unloading the old scene.
Forward references resolve through scoped pending tokens; missing authored references retain reported-null policy, while explicit live references validate against final state.
Replacing a scene stages destruction and creation together. Persistent roots survive, completed snapshots/clocks remain separate, and failed activation emits no lifecycle events.
Succeeding activation publishes destruction notifications, reverse-load-order scene unload summaries, then SceneReady. Regression expectations explicitly encode this order.

Native scene resources are decoded into an owned dependency union, including emitter-prefab dependencies, preflighted for capacity and staged for controller validation. World registrations occur only after the scene commit.
Project gravity/modules, input/residency and asset ownership update after successful native activation; this does not make the outer whole-project/persistent-startup workflow one atomic operation.
Editor reload retains old identity maps, remembered description and residency on rejection. Render preview staging also uses prepared activation.
Six added regressions cover replace/additive rollback/retry, retiring-target rejection, immediate prefab rollback, prepared resource publication, capacity rollback, and preview reload recovery.

Initial qualification caught a reused additive-scene ID in a new fixture and a complex staging result type. The fixture now reaches payload validation and the staging result is a named structure. Expanded stripped-feature coverage also found a legacy collision test missing its physics feature condition; its default-feature assertions remain unchanged. Failed attempts are retained.

Unavailable dependencies retain existing load diagnostics rather than introducing asynchronous readiness guarantees. Callback scene-load guards, runtime material/mesh/clip mutations, editor data/resource edits and cache/performance qualification remain open.
